semantics.kind: combinational; outputs follow input without clock or latency
semantics.evidence: Original problem defines each output directly from the input vector and specifies no clock, reset, or state.
semantics.out_both: For i=0..98, in[i] AND in[i+1]; bit 99 is constant zero.
semantics.out_any: For i=1..99, in[i] OR in[i-1]; bit 0 is constant zero.
semantics.out_different: For i=0..98, in[i] XOR in[i+1]; bit 99 is in[99] XOR in[0].
semantics.reset_initialization: No reset or stored initialization is specified or required; no registers.

numeric.index_direction: Left neighbour is the next larger index; right neighbour is the next smaller index.
numeric.operations: One-bit Boolean gates, with no arithmetic or signedness dependence.

verification.oracle: Per-bit loop based on the original neighbour descriptions, independent of DUT concatenations.
verification.sampling: Drive vector then allow one simulation time unit for combinational settling.
verification.cases: All zeros, all ones, alternating patterns, each single set and cleared bit, exhaustive local adjacent pair combinations, deterministic random vectors.
verification.failure: $fatal for any output mismatch; bounded timeout; PASS only at completion.

specification_ambiguities: Original problem does not specify X/Z behavior; ordinary bitwise gate propagation is used, with supplemental four-state checks but no claim of a separate required X/Z contract.
